paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: relief is not the same as surrender. The frogs were gone, the houses were quiet, and Pharaoh had said he would let the people go. Then, "When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, however, he hardened his heart" (Exodus 8:15). The same pattern shows up in us. We say big things when the frogs are on the bed, and we get real forgetful when the room clears out.

Now look at the other side. Moses said the frogs would go "so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God" (Exodus 8:10). The magicians could copy the frogs, but they couldn't make a single gnat, and they said, "This is the finger of God" (Exodus 8:19). Even Pharaoh's own people saw it. Somebody can see exactly who is in charge and still decide not to listen, and the text says that is what Pharaoh did.

So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today, baker. When God makes something plain to you, don't wait for the next plague to act on it. I spent years in a drawer, and I can tell you the LORD doesn't need our timing to be good, but He's glad when we answer Him quick. Obey while it's easy, friend, because the relief is a gift and not a loophole. And this story is not over yet.
